This code snippet iterates through a collection of numbers (`nums`) and builds a frequency map (histogram) using a Python dictionary. For each element `n`, it increments its count, defaulting to `0` if the key is not yet present in the dictionary via `counts.get(n, 0)`. This is a classic frequency-counting pattern.

The central mechanism relies on a dictionary (`counts`) to provide constant-time lookups and updates for counting occurrences of elements.
